transcript:
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
The White House is set to announce the construction of a steel mill in Iowa that it says will
be the largest ever in the United States.
NPR's Deepa Chivaram reports the construction and operation of the plant is expected to
create about 2,000 new permanent jobs.
Trump's announcement comes as Americans are souring on how they view Trump's handling
of the economy.
And with the midterm elections just a little over a month away, the president is running
out of time to shift voters' perspectives.
The steel plant is being built by Masabi Metallics, a company based in Minnesota, though the plant
will be constructed in Iowa.
It's expected to produce 10 million tons of steel a year once it's fully built.
The $15 billion investment marks the first mega-steel plant to be built in the U.S. since
the 1960s, according to the White House.
Deepa Chivaram, NPR News, the White House.
The U.S. ambassador to China, David Perdue, says President Trump asked Chinese President
Xi Jinping if he wanted to buy weapons from the U.S.
Perdue spoke to Fox News Sunday, days after Xi made his first state visit to the U.S.
in over a decade.
He did not specify when Trump made the arms sale offer to Xi.
The FBI is losing a deputy director for the second time since President Trump returned
to office.
NPR's Ryan Lucas reports Andrew Bailey has been on the job for a little more than a year.
Andrew Bailey says in a post on X that he is stepping down to return to his family in
Missouri.
But he says he's confident that Director Cash Patel will continue the work, including reforming
the FBI and combating violent crime.
Patel thanked Bailey for his service on X as well.
Bailey, a former attorney general for the state of Missouri, joined the FBI last August
under an unusual arrangement as co-deputy director alongside Dan Bongino, a right-wing
former podcast host.
Bongino left the bureau in January.
Now Bailey, too, is departing.
It's unclear whether he will be replaced.
The current remaining deputy director is a career special agent, which was the norm until
the second Trump administration.
Ryan Lucas, NPR News, Washington.
SpaceX's Starship rocket reached orbit today for the first time, but Central Florida Public
Media's Brendan Byrne reports a mission was cut short.
Starship and its 33-engine booster launched from SpaceX's Starbase in Texas on a planned
10-hour mission.
The launch, for the most part, went as designed.
An engine on Starship did shut down about 30 seconds early, but Mission Control decided
it was still safe to continue its orbital path.
Just about three hours after liftoff, it splashed down the Pacific Ocean near Hawaii.
It's unclear what caused the mission to end early.
During its time in orbit, Starship deployed more than two dozen Starlink satellites, a
new version that will help build SpaceX's global internet constellation in orbit.
SpaceX is counting on Starship to grow its commercial business, and NASA has tapped the
spacecraft to bring its astronauts to the lunar surface for future Artemis missions.
For NPR News, I'm Brendan Byrne in Orlando.
It's NPR.
Britain is investigating a suspected terrorism plot against an air force base used by the
U.S. military.
Authorities say five men were arrested.
Authorities have yet to disclose the charges or whether they have anything to do with the
U.S. war with Iran, Iran's embassy in London denies any involvement.
The U.S. and Iran have been at war for seven months now.
Both continue to battle for control of the Strait of Hormuz.
The most recent data by Kepler shows a seven-day average last week of around 13 million barrels
a day compared to 50 to 17 million barrels before the war.
Pope Leo XIV is urging Europe to find a way to secure peace, as NPR's Eleanor Beardsley
reports the American-born pontiff spent his final day in France in a city that is symbolic
of post-World War II reconciliation in Europe.
Pope Leo spoke in the city of Mess in the Alsace-Lorraine region long disputed by France
and Germany.
"Today, unfortunately, war has come again to Europe," he said, "where pointless massacres
are taking civilian lives."
Leo said Europe can stop the spiral of violence.
"You have demonstrated over the past 80 years of peace that it's possible to express divergent
opinions, demands, and interests through dialogue rather than confrontation," he said.
The pope also called on Europe to welcome those fleeing persecution and wars.
"That means integrating them as if into your own family," he said.
The pope called the migrants' arrival in Europe an exceptional encounter between peoples
and cultures.
I'm Eleanor Beardsley reporting, it's N.P.

topics.text: White House announces construction of largest U.S. steel mill in Iowa by Masabi Metallics
U.S. Ambassador David Perdue says Trump asked Chinese President Xi about buying U.S. weapons
FBI Deputy Director Andrew Bailey steps down after little over a year in position
SpaceX Starship rocket reaches orbit for first time, deploys Starlink satellites before early splashdown
Britain investigating suspected terrorism plot against air force base used by U.S. military, arrests five men
Pope Francis urges Europe to secure peace during final day in France, speaks in Alsace-Lorraine
